text: Why do you talk to me of brothers? You know that, as well as I.” “Attend to what I do know, and you may not,” said Mr. Brownlow. “I shall interest you by and by. I know that of the wretched marriage, into which family pride, and the most sordid and narrowest of all ambition, forced your unhappy father when a mere boy, you were the sole and most unnatural issue.” “I don’t care for hard names,” interrupted Monks with a jeering laugh. “You know the fact, and that’s enough for me.” “But I also know,” pursued the old gentleman, “the misery, the slow torture, the protracted anguish of that ill-assorted union.
